slides.text: AI Updates - Computing IBM and HSBC used Quantum Computers to improve trading IBM Heron quantum processor was used to enhance algorithmic bond trading - up to a 34% improvement in predicting the likelihood that bond trades would be completed at quoted prices This was done by combining quantum and classical computational methods on real-world, production-scale bond trading data This represents the world's first empirical evidence of quantum computing's practical value in financial services. This is "ground breaking world first" example https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/hsbc-algorithmic-bond-trading Netflix: monolithic architectures can scale Microservices impose a recurring "network tax" due to serialization, deserialization, additional network hops, and frequent retries and timeouts, all of which can impact latency and reliability; Debugging distributed traces becomes a nightmare, as diagnosing single requests can mean traversing hundreds of interconnected microservices, making root-cause analysis more difficult than in a monolithic setup Netflix’s practical experience with microservices exposes limitations and points out that, for some environments, monolithic systems can offer superior scalability and operational simplicity compared to highly distributed architectures https://medium.com/@yashbatra11111/how-netflix-accidentally-proved-monoliths-scale-better-than-microservices-f2d66f0a0bb5 StoneMQ - Open-source Messaging in Rust 6x times faster and 70% cheaper than Kafka Kafka Compatible, efficient scaling, loging/tracing Fully open source under the Apache 2.0 license https://github.com/jonefeewang/stonemq RAG python modules pip install RAGchain # pipelines, benchmarking, ... pip install raglight pip install rag light pip install flashrag-dev --pre pip install metagpt[rag] https://pypi.org/project/RAGchain/ https://python.langchain.com/docs/tutorials/rag/ https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/FlashRAG https://docs.deepwisdom.ai/main/en/guide/in_depth_guides/rag_module.html https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BfBLSnRKWMY https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mEmUN4lgpaU https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/get_started/ https://github.com/pymupdf/RAG

slides.title: Richard Sutton - Father of RL about LLMs
slides.text: Richard Sutton - Father of RL about LLMs Richard Sutton on Reinforcement Learning vs. LLMs LLMs mimic what people say, not what actually happens in the world RL is about learning from direct experience and consequences LLMs: lack true goals and ground truth for evaluating actions. Without goals, there's no "right" thing to do - just patterns to copy don't have a world model. They predict what people would say, not what will happen can not be surprised by outcomes or update based on unexpected events don't learn from life experiences as all mammals do The RL Alternative: Policy (what to do in each situation) Value function (how well things are going, learned via TD learning) State representation (perception/understanding of current situation) Transition model (predicting consequences of actions) Generalization: Current deep learning generalizes poorly and unpredictably Gradient descent solves problems but doesn't ensure good generalization to new situations Humans sculpt representations that transfer well; it's not automatic Catastrophic interference when learning new things is evidence of poor generalization Bitter Lesson: general methods which leverage computation consistently outperform methods based on human-crafted, domain-specific knowledge Sutton expects experience-based learning to eventually supersede LLM approaches, same pattern has repeated throughout AI history Infants learn through trial-and-error, not imitation or supervised learning; Supervised learning "doesn't happen in nature" - no examples of "correct" behavior exist; Understanding squirrels would get us most of the way to understanding human intelligence Transition to AI/augmented humans is inevitable (lack of unified governance, eventual understanding of intelligence, superintelligence development, and resource accumulation); Represents major universal transition from replication to design; Should view AIs as humanity's offspring rather than adversaries; Current world is "pretty bad" - openness to change is appropriate

slides.title: Evaluate AI for Production Peter Yang about AI
slides.text: Evaluate AI for Production Peter Yang about AI Evaluations Hamel Husain - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uiza7wp1KrE Aman Khan - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TL527yTpxlk Start with manual review of ~100 real product traces . Hand-annotate failures and pain points using open coding - this provides far more insight than jumping straight to metrics or automation. Export observations to a spreadsheet and use LLMs to cluster issues into categories like "handoff failures" or "conversation flow problems." Core Evaluation Types: Code-based, automated (e.g., prohibited term detection) Human evals by PM/expert with clear rubrics LLM-as-a-judge - automated, mimics human judgment User evals - real production feedback and business metrics Building Effective Evaluations: Create explicit prompts with all context variables defined Generate initial examples using realistic queries Build golden datasets through manual PM testing Develop clear rubrics (product knowledge, policy compliance, tone) Binary Over Continuous Scoring! Use pass/fail metrics, not 1-5 scales. Binary judgments are actionable—average scores like 3.2 vs 3.7 create ambiguity. Always ask: " Was this failure present? Yes or no." Validate LLM judges against human labels using confusion matrices, measure true positive/negative rates, not just agreement equire binary answers plus explanations from LLM evaluators Start with 5-10 examples for iteration, scale to 100+ for production confidence Operationalization Automate reliable judges - to run against production traces with dashboard monitoring. Maintain continuous human annotation, especially after significant changes. Keep tooling simple—use spreadsheets and built-in LLM tools for accessibility. Let categories emerge from real data, not hypotheses Regular lightweight manual checking maintains quality Small datasets enable fast iteration cycles Human judgment remains the gold standard for LLM-as-judge calibration Update rubrics and datasets as products and policies evolve This approach blends manual insight with scalable automation, ensuring evaluations remain both trustworthy and actionable for AI product development.

slides.title: Rust instead of Python Today production AI inference
slides.text: Rust instead of Python Today production AI inference is mostly done using Nvidia GPUS via  C++ CUDA libraries and Python for orchestration Python offers rapid iteration, broad library support, and ease of integration, while C++ / CUDA used for speed But Rust provides compelling alternative for production: https://medium.com/@theopinionatedev/rusts-ai-libraries-are-finally-beating-python-at-its-own-game-8f84dd26ccc4 Problems with Python: Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), large runtime footprints making edge deployment difficult, and the complexities of bundling Python with native C++ and CUDA libraries Rust's AI libraries are now surpassing Python’s for production, real-time inference, and edge AI due to Rust’s concurrency, efficiency, and simpler deployment However, Python continues to lead in research and academia https://medium.com/@theopinionatedev/rusts-ai-libraries-are-finally-beating-python-at-its-own-game-8f84dd26ccc4 Vendor Languages Used GPU Stack/Frameworks OpenAI Python, C++, CUDA CUDA, Triton, custom backend Anthropic Python, C/C++, CUDA Docker, Bazel, AWS Nitro Gemini Python, C++, Java, CUDA, TPU Custom Google stack (TPU), CUDA Perplexity Python, C++, CUDA NVIDIA Triton, TensorRT-LLM Mistral Python, C++, CUDA vLLM, open-source inference Qwen Python, C++, CUDA Alibaba custom backend, GQA Deepseek Python, C++, CUDA MoE optimization, CUDA Nvidia Python, C++, CUDA TensorRT, Triton Inference Server Rust Libraries: tch-rs - PyTorch C++ bindings in Rust tract - Pure Rust inference engine burn - Pure Rust deep learning framework linfa - Scikit-learn style ML for Rust onnxruntime-rs - Bindings to ONNXRuntime Apple is rewriting key parts of iOS in Rust-like languages for safety and performance - fewer crashes, better security, and maybe the start of a Rust-shaped future for iOS developers. https://medium.com/@devlinktips/apple-is-quietly-rewriting-ios-and-its-not-in-swift-or-objective-c-4af4dc578775
